I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I move a little if I think it will pay. I have 13.1 mu, and money is never loose, but I still would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. Around here, if wheat looks thin in spring, people regret saving one bag, not regret using it. I will keep most land in the wheat-maize turn because that is steady and I have well water, and I will keep some cotton because I know how to manage it and it spreads my risk. I do not like fancy changes. If a seed did well on nearby fields, I will use that kind. For wheat, I will feed it enough to push tillers and fill grain, with three waterings if the season stays normal. After wheat, I will put maize on the same land and keep the stubble work simple so I save labor. For cotton, I will use a little more potash and spray more times because if worms and aphids get ahead, cotton suffers fast. I will count every bag, but I will not cut too hard on inputs this year.
